parsed_answer.content:
Spring Boot Actuator is a production-ready module designed to help monitor, manage, and inspect Spring Boot applications in real-time. In a distributed microservice architecture, gaining visibility into application health, internal metrics, and memory usage without restarting or SSHing into production nodes is essential. Actuator brings production-grade telemetry directly to your runtime environment by exposing pre-built HTTP endpoints or JMX beans.

To effectively operate applications at scale, engineers rely heavily on several critical Actuator endpoints. The `/health` endpoint aggregates application liveness and readiness states, pulling data from underlying components like database connection pools, disk space, and custom health indicators. The `/metrics` endpoint taps into Micrometer, exposing dimensional runtime statistics such as JVM garbage collection pauses, HTTP request latencies, CPU utilization, and thread pool usage. Finally, the `/heapdump` endpoint captures a complete memory snapshot (HPROF binary file) of the running JVM heap, allowing engineers to diagnose complex memory leaks and out-of-memory errors offline using tools like Eclipse MAT or VisualVM.

rows: Returns application up/down status and subsystem health checks.
Low risk; frequently exposed internally to orchestrators like Kubernetes.
Exposes time-series performance data via Micrometer integration.
Medium risk; high cardinality tags can cause memory pressure.
Downloads a binary HPROF memory snapshot of the JVM heap.
High risk; blocking operation that can cause STW pauses and high I/O.

items: Actuator endpoints are auto-configured when spring-boot-starter-actuator is on the classpath, but by default, most endpoints (except /health and /info) are restricted to prevent sensitive data exposure.
The /health endpoint utilizes a hierarchical CompositeHealthContributor model, segregating liveness (/health/liveness) and readiness (/health/readiness) probes for Kubernetes container orchestration.
The /metrics endpoint acts as a facade over Micrometer, decoupling the metric recording instrumentation from underlying monitoring backends like Prometheus, Datadog, or New Relic.
Generating a /heapdump triggers a full Garbage Collection cycle prior to dumping the heap, which forces a massive Stop-The-World (STW) pause on large heaps, potentially timing out load balancers.

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: "health,metrics,heapdump"
      base-path: "/manage"
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: "always"
      probes:
        enabled: true
    heapdump:
      enabled: true

Senior Production Gotcha: Never expose Actuator endpoints on the same port as your business web traffic (server.port) in public-facing architectures. Always configure management.server.port to run Actuator on an isolated internal port or network interface, and secure it via Spring Security. Exposing /heapdump publicly is an immediate remote disclosure vulnerability that leaks sensitive user session data, database credentials, and cached entities residing in the JVM heap.
